patch_description: Treat the broadcast as a multicast (Steiner-tree-like) problem rather than independent per-destination shortest paths. Total cost depends on the union of edges used, so if a later destination can reach an already-delivered intermediate node cheaply and then reuse an already-paid edge prefix, the overall cost drops. Concretely: route destinations sequentially; after each destination is routed, mark its edges as "paid". For subsequent destinations, run Dijkstra on a reduced-cost graph where paid edges cost ~0 marginal (small epsilon to prefer shorter reuse), so routing strongly prefers reusing existing broadcast edges. This creates a shared multicast tree instead of parallel per-destination paths, reducing redundant transfers and total cost.
